sanskrit: tathā dhanapater yakṣā guhyakā rākṣasās tathā gandharvāpsarasaś caiva bhagavāṃś ca vṛṣadhvajaḥ
english: Likewise the yakṣas and guhyakas of Kubera, the lord of wealth, and the rākṣasas, the gandharvas and apsarases, and the blessed one whose banner bears the bull—all these are present there.

sanskrit: pitāmahasabhāyāṃ tu kathitās te maharṣayaḥ sarvadevanikāyāś ca sarvaśāstrāṇi caiva hi
english: In the assembly hall of Pitāmaha, O sage, the great sages were described to you, as were all the hosts of the gods and all the śāstras as well.

sanskrit: śatakratusabhāyāṃ tu devāḥ saṃkīrtitā mune uddeśataś ca gandharvā vividhāś ca maharṣayaḥ
english: In the assembly of Śatakratu, O sage, the gods were enumerated, and in summary the gandharvas of various kinds and the great sages.

sanskrit: eka eva tu rājarṣir hariścandro mahāmune kathitas te sabhānityo devendrasya mahātmanaḥ
english: But only one royal sage, the great-souled Hariścandra, O great sage, was described to you as a permanent resident of the assembly of the great Indra, lord of gods.

sanskrit: kiṃ karma tenācaritaṃ tapo vā niyatavratam yenāsau saha śakreṇa spardhate sma mahāyaśāḥ
english: What deed did he perform, or what austerity and firm vow, by which he, the greatly renowned one, could rival even Śakra himself?

sanskrit: pitṛlokagataś cāpi tvayā vipra pitā mama dṛṣṭaḥ pāṇḍur mahābhāgaḥ kathaṃ cāsi samāgataḥ
english: And, O brahmin, my greatly fortunate father Pāṇḍu, who has gone to the realm of the ancestors, was also seen by you — how did you come to meet him?

sanskrit: kim uktavāṃś ca bhagavann etad icchāmi veditum tvattaḥ śrotum ahaṃ sarvaṃ paraṃ kautūhalaṃ hi me
english: And what did he say, O blessed one? I wish to know this. I have the greatest curiosity to hear everything from you.

sanskrit: nārada uvāca yan māṃ pṛcchasi rājendra hariścandraṃ prati prabho tat te 'haṃ saṃpravakṣyāmi māhātmyaṃ tasya dhīmataḥ
english: Nārada said: O king of kings, O lord, since you ask me about Hariścandra, I shall fully declare to you the greatness of that wise one.

sanskrit: sa rājā balavān āsīt samrāṭ sarvamahīkṣitām tasya sarve mahīpālāḥ śāsanāvanatāḥ sthitāḥ
english: That king was mighty, an emperor over all rulers of the earth; all the guardians of the earth stood bowing in obedience to his commands.

sanskrit: tenaikaṃ ratham āsthāya jaitraṃ hemavibhūṣitam śastrapratāpena jitā dvīpāḥ sapta nareśvara
english: Mounting a single victorious chariot adorned with gold, he conquered by the might of his weapons all seven continents, O lord of men.

sanskrit: sa vijitya mahīṃ sarvāṃ saśailavanakānanām ājahāra mahārāja rājasūyaṃ mahākratum
english: Having conquered the entire earth with its mountains, forests, and woodlands, O great king, he performed the Rājasūya, that great sacrifice.

sanskrit: tasya sarve mahīpālā dhanāny ājahrur ājñayā dvijānāṃ pariveṣṭāras tasmin yajñe ca te 'bhavan
english: At his command all the guardians of the earth brought their wealth, and they served as attendants to the twice-born at that sacrifice.

sanskrit: prādāc ca draviṇaṃ prītyā yājakānāṃ nareśvaraḥ yathoktaṃ tatra tais tasmiṃs tataḥ pañcaguṇādhikam
english: With joy the lord of men gave wealth to the officiating priests, giving five times more than what they had prescribed.

sanskrit: atarpayac ca vividhair vasubhir brāhmaṇāṃs tathā prāsarpakāle saṃprāpte nānādigbhyaḥ samāgatān
english: He also satisfied the brāhmaṇas, who had come from all directions, with varied goods and riches when the time of distribution arrived.

sanskrit: bhakṣyair bhojyaiś ca vividhair yathākāmapuraskṛtaiḥ ratnaughatarpitais tuṣṭair dvijaiś ca samudāhṛtam tejasvī ca yaśasvī ca nṛpebhyo 'bhyadhiko 'bhavat
english: With various foods and eatables offered according to desire, and with floods of gems by which the twice-born were satisfied and gladdened — thus it was declared — he became radiant and glorious, superior to all other kings.

sanskrit: etasmāt kāraṇāt pārtha hariścandro virājate tebhyo rājasahasrebhyas tad viddhi bharatarṣabha
english: For this reason, O Pārtha, Hariścandra shines above those thousands of kings — know this, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: samāpya ca hariścandro mahāyajñaṃ pratāpavān abhiṣiktaḥ sa śuśubhe sāmrājyena narādhipa
english: And Hariścandra the splendid, having completed the great sacrifice, was consecrated and shone with imperial sovereignty, O lord of men.

sanskrit: ye cānye 'pi mahīpālā rājasūyaṃ mahākratum yajante te mahendreṇa modante saha bhārata
english: And those other guardians of the earth who have performed the Rājasūya, that great sacrifice, rejoice together with the great Indra, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: ye cāpi nidhanaṃ prāptāḥ saṃgrāmeṣv apalāyinaḥ te tatsadaḥ samāsādya modante bharatarṣabha
english: And those who have met their death on battlefields without fleeing — they, having reached that assembly, rejoice, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: tapasā ye ca tīvreṇa tyajantīha kalevaram te 'pi tat sthānam āsādya śrīmanto bhānti nityaśaḥ
english: And those who abandon their bodies here through intense austerity — they too, having attained that place, shine in splendor eternally.

sanskrit: pitā ca tvāha kaunteya pāṇḍuḥ kauravanandanaḥ hariścandre śriyaṃ dṛṣṭvā nṛpatau jātavismayaḥ
english: And your father, Pāṇḍu, O son of Kuntī, O delight of the Kauravas, having seen the glory of the royal sage Hariścandra, was filled with wonder and said to you:

sanskrit: samartho 'si mahīṃ jetuṃ bhrātaras te vaśe sthitāḥ rājasūyaṃ kratuśreṣṭham āharasveti bhārata
english: "You are capable of conquering the earth, your brothers stand under your command — perform the Rājasūya, the foremost of sacrifices, O Bhārata."

sanskrit: tasya tvaṃ puruṣavyāghra saṃkalpaṃ kuru pāṇḍava gantāras te mahendrasya pūrvaiḥ saha salokatām
english: Fulfill his wish, O tiger among men, O son of Pāṇḍu — you shall go to share the same world as the great Indra together with your ancestors.

sanskrit: bahuvighnaś ca nṛpate kratur eṣa smṛto mahān chidrāṇy atra hi vāñchanti yajñaghnā brahmarākṣasāḥ
english: This great sacrifice is remembered as full of many obstacles, O king; for the brahma-rākṣasas who destroy sacrifices seek loopholes in it.

sanskrit: yuddhaṃ ca pṛṣṭhagamanaṃ pṛthivīkṣayakārakam kiṃ cid eva nimittaṃ ca bhavaty atra kṣayāvaham
english: Battle, retreat, and the destruction of the earth — some occasion for ruin arises here as well.

sanskrit: etat saṃcintya rājendra yat kṣamaṃ tat samācara apramattotthito nityaṃ cāturvarṇyasya rakṣaṇe bhava edhasva modasva dānais tarpaya ca dvijān
english: Having considered all this, O king of kings, do what is proper. Be ever vigilant and active in protecting the four social orders; prosper, rejoice, and satisfy the twice-born with gifts.

sanskrit: etat te vistareṇoktaṃ yan māṃ tvaṃ paripṛcchasi āpṛcche tvāṃ gamiṣyāmi dāśārhanagarīṃ prati
english: This has been told to you in full, all that you asked of me. I take leave of you; I shall go to the city of the Dāśārhas.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam ākhyāya pārthebhyo nārado janamejaya jagāma tair vṛto rājann ṛṣibhir yaiḥ samāgataḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having thus narrated to the sons of Pṛthā, O Janamejaya, O king, Nārada departed, accompanied by those same sages with whom he had arrived.

sanskrit: gate tu nārade pārtho bhrātṛbhiḥ saha kaurava rājasūyaṃ kratuśreṣṭhaṃ cintayām āsa bhārata
english: When Nārada had departed, the son of Pṛthā, together with his brothers, O Kaurava, began to contemplate the Rājasūya, the foremost of sacrifices, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca ṛṣes tad vacanaṃ śrutvā niśaśvāsa yudhiṣṭhiraḥ cintayan rājasūyāptiṃ na lebhe śarma bhārata
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the sage's words, Yudhiṣṭhira sighed deeply; pondering the attainment of the Rājasūya, he found no peace, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: rājarṣīṇāṃ hi taṃ śrutvā mahimānaṃ mahātmanām yajvanāṃ karmabhiḥ puṇyair lokaprāptiṃ samīkṣya ca
english: For having heard that greatness of the great-souled royal sages, and having looked upon the attainment of the celestial world by sacrificers through their meritorious deeds,

sanskrit: hariścandraṃ ca rājarṣiṃ rocamānaṃ viśeṣataḥ yajvānaṃ yajñam āhartuṃ rājasūyam iyeṣa saḥ
english: and seeing above all the royal sage Hariścandra shining brilliantly, the sacrificer — he desired to perform the sacrifice, the Rājasūya.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhiras tataḥ sarvān arcayitvā sabhāsadaḥ pratyarcitaś ca taiḥ sarvair yajñāyaiva mano dadhe
english: Then Yudhiṣṭhira, having honored all the members of the assembly, and having been honored by all of them in return, set his mind firmly upon the sacrifice.

sanskrit: sa rājasūyaṃ rājendra kurūṇām ṛṣabhaḥ kratum āhartuṃ pravaṇaṃ cakre manaḥ saṃcintya so 'sakṛt
english: He, the bull of the Kurus, O king of kings, turned his mind, thinking it over again and again, toward performing the Rājasūya sacrifice.

sanskrit: bhūyaś cādbhutavīryaujā dharmam evānupālayan kiṃ hitaṃ sarvalokānāṃ bhaved iti mano dadhe
english: And he who possessed marvelous strength and vigor, ever upholding dharma, set his mind upon what would be beneficial for all the worlds.

sanskrit: anugṛhṇan prajāḥ sarvāḥ sarvadharmavidāṃ varaḥ aviśeṣeṇa sarveṣāṃ hitaṃ cakre yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Extending favor to all his subjects without distinction, Yudhiṣṭhira, the foremost among all who know dharma, acted for the welfare of all.

sanskrit: evaṃ gate tatas tasmin pitarīvāśvasañ janāḥ na tasya vidyate dveṣṭā tato 'syājātaśatrutā
english: Things being thus, people took confidence in him as if he were their father; he had no enemy — hence his epithet Ajātaśatru, "he who has no born enemy."

sanskrit: sa mantriṇaḥ samānāyya bhrātṝṃś ca vadatāṃ varaḥ rājasūyaṃ prati tadā punaḥ punar apṛcchata
english: He, the foremost among speakers, summoned his ministers and his brothers and consulted them again and again about the Rājasūya.

sanskrit: te pṛcchyamānāḥ sahitā vaco 'rthyaṃ mantriṇas tadā yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahāprājñaṃ yiyakṣum idam abruvan
english: The ministers, thus questioned together, then spoke this purposeful reply to Yudhiṣṭhira, the greatly wise one who desired to sacrifice:

sanskrit: yenābhiṣikto nṛpatir vāruṇaṃ guṇam ṛcchati tena rājāpi san kṛtsnaṃ samrāḍguṇam abhīpsati
english: "The king who is consecrated with this rite attains the quality of Varuṇa; even being already a king, he seeks to attain the full quality of an emperor.

sanskrit: tasya samrāḍguṇārhasya bhavataḥ kurunandana rājasūyasya samayaṃ manyante suhṛdas tava
english: Your friends consider the time for the Rājasūya to have come for you, O delight of the Kurus, you who are worthy of the qualities of an emperor.

sanskrit: tasya yajñasya samayaḥ svādhīnaḥ kṣatrasaṃpadā sāmnā ṣaḍ agnayo yasmiṃś cīyante saṃśitavrataiḥ
english: The occasion for that sacrifice is under your own control through the wealth of the kṣatriya; with the Sāman hymn, the six fires are built up therein by those of firm vows.

sanskrit: darvīhomān upādāya sarvān yaḥ prāpnute kratūn abhiṣekaṃ ca yajñānte sarvajit tena cocyate
english: He who, taking up the oblations with the ladle, completes all the rites and undergoes the consecration at the sacrifice's end — he is called the conqueror of all.

sanskrit: samartho 'si mahābāho sarve te vaśagā vayam avicārya mahārāja rājasūye manaḥ kuru
english: You are capable, O mighty-armed one; we all stand under your command — without hesitation, O great king, set your mind upon the Rājasūya."

sanskrit: ity evaṃ suhṛdaḥ sarve pṛthak ca saha cābruvan sa dharmyaṃ pāṇḍavas teṣāṃ vacaḥ śrutvā viśāṃ pate dhṛṣṭam iṣṭaṃ variṣṭhaṃ ca jagrāha manasārihā
english: Thus all friends spoke, both separately and together; the son of Pāṇḍu, O lord of the people, hearing their words — so righteous, bold, dear, and most excellent — embraced them with his mind, he the slayer of foes.

sanskrit: śrutvā suhṛdvacas tac ca jānaṃś cāpy ātmanaḥ kṣamam punaḥ punar mano dadhre rājasūyāya bhārata
english: Having heard those friends' words and knowing also what was fitting for himself, he set his mind upon the Rājasūya again and again, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: sa bhrātṛbhiḥ punar dhīmān ṛtvigbhiś ca mahātmabhiḥ dhaumyadvaipāyanādyaiś ca mantrayām āsa mantribhiḥ
english: The wise one then again deliberated with his brothers, with the great-souled officiating priests, and with ministers headed by Dhaumya and Dvaipāyana.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca iyaṃ yā rājasūyasya samrāḍarhasya sukratoḥ śraddadhānasya vadataḥ spṛhā me sā kathaṃ bhavet
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: This desire that I have for the Rājasūya — of one worthy of imperial rank, of pure intention and faith — how might it come to be fulfilled?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca evam uktās tu te tena rājñā rājīvalocana idam ūcur vacaḥ kāle dharmātmānaṃ yudhiṣṭhiram arhas tvam asi dharmajña rājasūyaṃ mahākratum
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus addressed by that king of lotus-like eyes, they spoke in due time these words to the righteous-souled Yudhiṣṭhira: "You are worthy, O knower of dharma, to perform the Rājasūya, that great sacrifice."

sanskrit: athaivam ukte nṛpatāv ṛtvigbhir ṛṣibhis tathā mantriṇo bhrātaraś cāsya tad vacaḥ pratyapūjayan
english: Then, when the king had been thus addressed by the officiating priests and sages, his ministers and brothers also honored those words with their approval.

sanskrit: sa tu rājā mahāprājñaḥ punar evātmanātmavān bhūyo vimamṛśe pārtho lokānāṃ hitakāmyayā
english: But that greatly wise king, master of himself, the son of Pṛthā, reflected again and again for the sake of what would be beneficial to the worlds.

sanskrit: sāmarthyayogaṃ saṃprekṣya deśakālau vyayāgamau vimṛśya samyak ca dhiyā kurvan prājño na sīdati
english: By examining the conjunction of capabilities, by properly weighing place and time, expenditure and income with discernment — the wise one who acts thus does not falter.

sanskrit: na hi yajñasamārambhaḥ kevalātmavipattaye bhavatīti samājñāya yatnataḥ kāryam udvahan
english: Understanding that the undertaking of a sacrifice does not lead merely to one's own ruin, he carried out what needed to be done with all diligence.

sanskrit: sa niścayārthaṃ kāryasya kṛṣṇam eva janārdanam sarvalokāt paraṃ matvā jagāma manasā harim
english: For the sake of resolving what must be done, he went in his mind to Kṛṣṇa Janārdana alone, considering Hari to be supreme above all the worlds.

sanskrit: aprameyaṃ mahābāhuṃ kāmāj jātam ajaṃ nṛṣu pāṇḍavas tarkayām āsa karmabhir devasaṃmitaiḥ
english: The son of Pāṇḍu reflected upon the immeasurable, mighty-armed one — the unborn who took birth among men by his own will — judging him by deeds equal to those of the gods.

sanskrit: nāsya kiṃ cid avijñātaṃ nāsya kiṃ cid akarmajam na sa kiṃ cin na viṣahed iti kṛṣṇam amanyata
english: "Nothing is unknown to him, nothing is born not of his doing; there is nothing he cannot endure" — thus he thought of Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: sa tu tāṃ naiṣṭhikīṃ buddhiṃ kṛtvā pārtho yudhiṣṭhiraḥ guruvad bhūtagurave prāhiṇod dūtam añjasā
english: Having thus made that firm resolution, Yudhiṣṭhira the son of Pṛthā straightway sent a messenger to the guru of all beings, honoring him as his own teacher.

sanskrit: śīghragena rathenāśu sa dūtaḥ prāpya yādavān dvārakāvāsinaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ dvāravatyāṃ samāsadat
english: That messenger, traveling swiftly with a fast chariot, reached the Yādavas and arrived at Dvārakā where Kṛṣṇa, dweller of Dvārakā, resided.

sanskrit: darśanākāṅkṣiṇaṃ pārthaṃ darśanākāṅkṣayācyutaḥ indrasenena sahita indraprasthaṃ yayau tadā
english: Acyuta, who longed to see the son of Pṛthā who longed to see him, then went with Indrasena to Indraprastha.

sanskrit: vyatītya vividhān deśāṃs tvarāvān kṣipravāhanaḥ indraprasthagataṃ pārtham abhyagacchaj janārdanaḥ
english: Passing through various lands with haste, his horses swift, Janārdana came to the son of Pṛthā who had gone to Indraprastha.

sanskrit: sa gṛhe bhrātṛvad bhrātrā dharmarājena pūjitaḥ bhīmena ca tato 'paśyat svasāraṃ prītimān pituḥ
english: He was honored in the household by Dharmarāja as if by a brother, and then joyfully he saw also Bhīma and his father's sister's son.

sanskrit: prītaḥ priyeṇa suhṛdā reme sa sahitas tadā arjunena yamābhyāṃ ca guruvat paryupasthitaḥ
english: Delighted, he then rejoiced together with his dear friend Arjuna and the twin sons of Yama, who attended upon him as upon a teacher.

sanskrit: taṃ viśrāntaṃ śubhe deśe kṣaṇinaṃ kalyam acyutam dharmarājaḥ samāgamya jñāpayat svaṃ prayojanam
english: When Acyuta had rested in that pleasant place and had a moment's leisure in the morning, Dharmarāja approached him and made known his own purpose.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca prārthito rājasūyo me na cāsau kevalepsayā prāpyate yena tat te ha viditaṃ kṛṣṇa sarvaśaḥ
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: The Rājasūya is desired by me, but it is not to be attained by mere desire alone; the means by which it is attained — that you know in full, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: yasmin sarvaṃ saṃbhavati yaś ca sarvatra pūjyate yaś ca sarveśvaro rājā rājasūyaṃ sa vindati
english: He in whom all qualities are present, who is honored everywhere, and who is the lord over all kings — such a king attains the Rājasūya.

sanskrit: taṃ rājasūyaṃ suhṛdaḥ kāryam āhuḥ sametya me tatra me niścitatamaṃ tava kṛṣṇa girā bhavet
english: My friends, having assembled, say that Rājasūya must be performed by me; let my most certain resolution in this be made by your words, O Kṛṣṇa.

sanskrit: ke cid dhi sauhṛdād eva doṣaṃ na paricakṣate arthahetos tathaivānye priyam eva vadanty uta
english: For some, out of friendship alone, do not point out faults; others likewise, for the sake of their own interests, speak only what is pleasing.

sanskrit: priyam eva parīpsante ke cid ātmani yad dhitam evaṃprāyāś ca dṛśyante janavādāḥ prayojane
english: Some seek only what is pleasing, according to what they consider beneficial for themselves — and such, for the most part, is how people's counsel is seen in matters of purpose.

sanskrit: tvaṃ tu hetūn atītyaitān kāmakrodhau vyatītya ca paramaṃ naḥ kṣamaṃ loke yathāvad vaktum arhasi
english: But you, transcending these motives and rising above desire and anger, ought to speak to us what is truly most fitting in the world.

sanskrit: śrīkṛṣṇa uvāca sarvair guṇair mahārāja rājasūyaṃ tvam arhasi jānatas tv eva te sarvaṃ kiṃ cid vakṣyāmi bhārata
english: Śrī Kṛṣṇa said: With all your qualities, O great king, you are worthy of the Rājasūya. Yet, knowing all this, I shall say something to you, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: jāmadagnyena rāmeṇa kṣatraṃ yad avaśeṣitam tasmād avarajaṃ loke yad idaṃ kṣatrasaṃjñitam
english: The kṣatriya class that Rāma son of Jamadagni left remaining — from that descended what is now known in the world as the kṣatriya order.

sanskrit: kṛto 'yaṃ kulasaṃkalpaḥ kṣatriyair vasudhādhipa nideśavāgbhis tat te ha viditaṃ bharatarṣabha
english: This resolve of the lineage was made by the kṣatriyas, O lord of the earth, with words of command — that you know well, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: ailasyekṣvākuvaṃśasya prakṛtiṃ paricakṣate rājānaḥ śreṇibaddhāś ca tato 'nye kṣatriyā bhuvi
english: The nature of the lineage of Aila and of the Ikṣvāku dynasty is described: kings standing in ranks, and from them the other kṣatriyas on earth.

sanskrit: ailavaṃśyās tu ye rājaṃs tathaivekṣvākavo nṛpāḥ tāni caikaśataṃ viddhi kulāni bharatarṣabha
english: Those kings descended from the Aila lineage and likewise those of the Ikṣvāku line — know those to be one hundred and one clans, O bull of the Bhāratas.

sanskrit: yayātes tv eva bhojānāṃ vistaro 'tiguṇo mahān bhajate ca mahārāja vistaraḥ sa caturdiśam
english: From Yayāti itself the great and greatly virtuous expansion of the Bhojas arose, and that expansion, O great king, extends in all four directions.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ tathaiva tāṃ lakṣmīṃ sarvakṣatram upāsate so 'vanīṃ madhyamāṃ bhuktvā mithobhedeṣv amanyata
english: All the kṣatriyas attend upon that prosperity of theirs likewise; he, having enjoyed the central earth, thought of it in terms of mutual division.

sanskrit: caturyus tv aparo rājā yasminn ekaśato 'bhavat sa sāmrājyaṃ jarāsaṃdhaḥ prāpto bhavati yonitaḥ
english: But Jarāsaṃdha is another king at whose yoke a hundred kings have become subservient; he has attained imperial sovereignty by his origin.

sanskrit: taṃ sa rājā mahāprājña saṃśritya kila sarvaśaḥ rājan senāpatir jātaḥ śiśupālaḥ pratāpavān
english: Relying entirely upon that king, O greatly wise one, O king, the mighty Śiśupāla has indeed become a commander of his armies.

sanskrit: tam eva ca mahārāja śiṣyavat samupasthitaḥ vakraḥ karūṣādhipatir māyāyodhī mahābalaḥ
english: And waiting upon him alone as if a pupil, O great king, is Vakra, the lord of Karūṣa, a warrior of illusion and great strength.

sanskrit: aparau ca mahāvīryau mahātmānau samāśritau jarāsaṃdhaṃ mahāvīryaṃ tau haṃsaḍibhakāv ubhau
english: And two others of great valor and great soul have taken refuge with the mighty Jarāsaṃdha — those two, Haṃsa and Ḍibhaka.
